newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Airline merger spotlight falls on KLM.
newsitem.headline: Airline merger spotlight falls on KLM.

text.p: A rash of new and rumoured airline hook-ups on Friday refocused attention on Dutch flag carrier KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV itself seeking a partner to bolster its loss-making European activities.
KLM said on Thursday president Pieter Bouw would take the unusual step during its first-half results news conference on November 5 to field queries unrelated to the airline's earnings.

Coming amid news of Spanish airline Iberia's alliance with one or more European carriers and Air France's U.S. code-sharing agreement, the statement kindled Dutch media speculation it could be poised to unveil a major partnership.
Potential alliance candidates include Spain's Iberia, British Airways and Swissair/Sabena, newspapers said.
KLM shares were up 30 cents at 43.30 by 0950 GMT, outperforming a slightly firmer Amsterdam bourse.
But analysts were cooler on the prospects of an imminent deal. "I don't think KLM will announce an alliance on November 5," said MeesPierson analyst Richard Brakenhoff.
He said Iberia, which previously confirmed it was in "intensive" talks with both KLM and British Airways, would make a perfect partner for KLM in Europe.
"Iberia would give KLM a (European) market share of well above (KLM's targeted) 10 percent," he said.
A KLM-Iberia link-up would also offer important synergies on South American routes, where both carriers had a significant presence, he noted.

Gert Jochems, airlines analyst with brokers NIB Strating, said this week's trans-Atlantic code-sharing pact between Air France and U.S. airlines Delta and Continental could open the way for renewed partnership talks between KLM and Swissair.
Swissair, Austrian Airlines and Sabena already operate a link-up with Delta, but Swissair could now conceivably look to sever the tie, opting instead for KLM's U.S. partner Northwest, Jochems said.
"KLM and Swissair have been in love for years," he said.

But Brakenhoff said such a scenario was unlikely, given that Alcazar, an ambitious attempt at a four-way link-up between KLM, Swissair, Scandinavian Airlines Systems (SAS) and Austrian Airlines foundered in 1983 over Swissair's reluctance to give up Delta in favour of Northwest.
"Delta is much, much bigger than Northwest," he said.
Both analysts dismissed as idle speculation fresh rumours of a tie-up between KLM and British Airways, after Virgin Atlantic boss Richard Branson accused the two of "cutting secret deals".
"KLM would be the poor relation in a BA-American Airlines alliance," Jochems said.
"British Airways is not interested in KLM," Brakenhoff agreed.
-- Lien van der Leij, A'dam newsroom +31 20 504 5000
